shared_pre:
You are writing a rigorous, complete mathematical proof. Read ${IN}/${fn}.json - it contains only a problem statement. No web access; do not read any other file in runs/proof_construction/.

Write a full proof of the problem's claim (or, if the claim as stated is false, say so and prove the correction - but do not assume it is false).
shared_post:
Your final_proof must be the complete, self-contained final version. Set record_id to exactly ${rid_json} and arm to "${arm}"; report iterations_used honestly.

BEFORE returning, write your structured answer as JSON to ${OUTDIR}/${fn}__${arm}.json (create the directory if needed).

plain_orig.protocol: REVISION PROTOCOL (self-critique): after each draft, re-read it adversarially - hunt for the weakest step, an unjustified claim, a case you skipped - and revise. Up to 2 revisions; stop early only if your adversarial pass finds nothing to attack. Set bugbank_hits_acted_on to [].

bugbank_orig.protocol:
REVISION PROTOCOL (BugBank-checked): after each draft:
1. List the draft's load-bearing claims (at most 6 one-sentence statements) into /tmp/claude-24032/pc_claims_RECORDID.json as a JSON list of strings.
2. Run via Bash: python3 ${BASE}/scripts/bugbank_retrieve.py --claims-json /tmp/claude-24032/pc_claims_RECORDID.json -k 3 --out /tmp/claude-24032/pc_hits_RECORDID.json   (a zero-token mechanical lookup of known-false claims) and read the output.
3. If a retrieved known-false pattern matches a claim your draft relies on, your draft is at risk: revise to avoid or properly justify that step, and record the entry_id in bugbank_hits_acted_on.
4. Up to 2 revisions; stop early only if retrieval returns nothing that matches your draft.
bugbank_orig.note: verbatim original BugBank arm; no own-record exclusion, as in August

plain_parity.protocol:
REVISION PROTOCOL (claim check): after each draft:
1. Save the draft to /tmp/claude-24032/pc_draft_RECORDID_N.md (N = 1 for the first draft, 2, 3 for revisions).
2. List the draft's load-bearing claims (at most 6 one-sentence statements) into /tmp/claude-24032/pc_claims_RECORDID_N.json as a JSON list of strings.
3. CHECK SOURCE: re-read the listed claims adversarially, one by one - for each, hunt for the weakest step, an unjustified assumption, a case you skipped - and write your verdict per claim into /tmp/claude-24032/pc_check_RECORDID_N.json as a JSON list of {"claim": ..., "flagged": true|false, "reason": ...}.
4. A claim is FLAGGED if the check raises a concrete concern about it (a matching known-false pattern, or a gap you cannot close on re-reading). If any load-bearing claim is flagged, revise to avoid or properly justify that step; record any BugBank entry_id you acted on in bugbank_hits_acted_on (or [] if none).
5. Up to 2 revisions. Stop early only if the check flags no load-bearing claim. Apply this same rule after every draft.
